statements.impact_statement: CVE-2014-8166 is in the legacy CUPS browsing protocol, which accepted shared printer names containing ANSI escape sequences from the network: https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1084577. Upstream removed that protocol in CUPS 1.6. Its CHANGES.txt says 'CUPS no longer supports automatic remote printers or implicit classes via the CUPS, LDAP, or SLP protocols (STR #3922, STR #3923)': https://github.com/apple/cups/blob/release-1.6.0/CHANGES.txt. The Red Hat bug likewise notes that the functionality was removed in CUPS 1.6. This package is built from CUPS 2.4.10. We checked the 2.4.10 source: scheduler/dirsvc.c no longer contains the browse receive code (process_browse_data, BrowseShortNames), and printer and class names added through scheduler/ipp.c must pass validate_name(), which rejects control characters including ESC. Ubuntu also records the code as removed in 1.6: https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2014-8166
